terms.comment: Traupman’s word. Classically īnstruere is to build in, then to equip, furnish or fit out (domum īnstruere, Cic. Verr. 2.4.9; convīvium, to lay on a dinner): installing a program is fitting out the computer with it. Its other everyday sense is to draw up troops in order (aciem īnstruere).

phrases.latin: Programma novum īnstrūxī; jam computātrum dēnuō excitandum est.
phrases.english: I’ve installed the new program; now the computer has to be restarted.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 261, 333.
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
